job.title: SEND Employability & Student Support Coordinator
job.description:
KC Group is delighted to be recruiting a SEND Employability & Student Support Coordinator on behalf of a leading further and higher education provider in Birmingham, to join them on a temporary, part-time basis and make a real, positive impact on student outcomes.

The role is based onsite, working approximately 30 hours per week, 6 hours per day, Monday-Friday, and paying an hourly rate of £16-17.12 per hour dependant on experience.

Due to the nature of this role, applicants must hold a valid Enhanced DBS certificate (ideally registered on the DBS Update Service).

As a SEND Employability & Student Support Coordinator, you will work closely with EHCP (Education, Health and Care Plan) students to help them access enrichment activities, develop essential social and communication skills, and successfully prepare for employment, apprenticeships, or further study.

Key responsibilities for the SEND Employability & Student Support Coordinator include:

  • Student Engagement: Collaborating with curriculum teams and support services to ensure students are fully integrated and engaged in inclusive college life.
  • Employability Support: Providing practical guidance to improve student employability, including CV writing, interview preparation, and motivational coaching.
  • Progress Tracking: Monitoring and tracking individual student development, participation, and progress.
  • Relationship Building: Building positive, motivating relationships with learners to foster confidence and independence.

To be successful as a SEND Employability & Student Support Coordinator, you will be a dedicated professional who shares a genuine passion for improving student outcomes and supporting individuals with additional needs.

  • Experience: Previous experience supporting learners with SEND, Special Educational Needs, EHCPs, or neurodiversity.
  • Skills: Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to motivate and inspire students.
  • Approach: Highly organised, proactive, and systematic with a strong focus on student-centred development.

If you are an experienced professional looking for a rewarding part-time SEND Employability & Student Support Coordinator opportunity within a thriving educational environment, apply today with your up-to-date CV! For more Information contact reiss@kateandco.com.

job.title: Case Handler
job.description:
KC Group are recruiting Case Handlers on behalf of a leading housing and property maintenance organisation In the Stratford Upon Avon area.

This is a temporary opportunity offering an hourly rate of £16.28 per hour, working full-time, Monday to Friday, with a hybrid working pattern.

We're looking for a Case Handler to take end-to-end ownership of housing hazard cases—ensuring reported issues are assessed promptly, prioritised by risk, and resolved safely within strict statutory timescales.

Key Responsibilities of the Case Handler role:

  • Managing HHSRS and Awaab's Law cases from initial referral through to compliant, evidenced closure.
  • Triaging reported hazards, assessing risk and customer vulnerability, and prioritising actions in line with legislation and policy.
  • Raising, instructing, and coordinating repair works with contractors and internal teams to ensure works are delivered to standard and within statutory timescales.
  • Coordinating proportionate interim measures—including decant arrangements where required—until a permanent resolution is achieved.
  • Acting as the main point of contact for customers throughout their case, making early contact, managing expectations, and confirming access arrangements.
  • Maintaining comprehensive, accurate case records and audit trails across internal IT systems.
  • Reviewing evidence of completed works to verify hazards are fully resolved prior to case closure, escalating any delays or quality concerns.
  • Assisting with Local Authority and Environmental Health liaison, tracking statutory notices and commitments through to completion.

To be considered for the Case Handler role:

  • Experience managing housing repairs, property compliance, technical, or customer-focused cases from referral to resolution.
  • Strong working knowledge of Awaab's Law, HHSRS, statutory repair obligations, and social housing regulatory requirements.
  • Good technical judgement to assess property defects, safeguard customers, and implement interim measures.
  • Excellent organisational, analytical, and case management skills, with the ability to balance competing priorities.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, able to explain technical information clearly to customers, contractors, and colleagues.
  • Strong IT skills with experience maintaining accurate records and clear compliance audit trails.
  • Understanding of repairs quality assurance within a regulated social housing environment (desirable).
  • Membership of, or willingness to work towards, a relevant professional body such as CIOB, RICS, or CIH (desirable).

Key information about the Case Handler role:

  • £16.28 per hour.
  • Full-time, Monday to Friday.
  • Hybrid working available
  • Temporary opportunity.
  • Supportive team environment.
  • Immediate start available.
  • Potential for longer-term opportunities.

For more information, contact Reiss on 0121 705 0077 or at reiss@kateandco.com or candy@kateandco.com
Should your application be unsuccessful, your CV will be kept on file and considered for future suitable opportunities.

job.title: Principle Manager (Compliance)
job.description:
An established public sector organisation is seeking an experienced Property Compliance Manager to lead a key area of its housing maintenance and property compliance service, helping to ensure its homes remain safe, compliant and well maintained.

This is a senior leadership opportunity within a large, customer-focused housing operation, responsible for maintaining and improving a substantial residential property portfolio. The organisation invests significantly in its housing stock, with a strong commitment to ensuring homes remain safe, compliant and maintained to a high standard.

You will lead a specialist safety and compliance function, taking overall responsibility for ensuring the organisation meets its statutory and regulatory obligations as a social housing landlord.

With a strong emphasis on continuous improvement, service delivery and resident safety, this is an excellent opportunity for an experienced professional to influence strategy, drive operational performance and make a meaningful difference to housing standards.

Key Responsibilities as a Property Compliance Manager:

  • Provide senior leadership and strategic oversight of housing maintenance safety and compliance.
  • Act as the lead responsible officer for ensuring residential properties remain safe and meet all relevant statutory and regulatory requirements.
  • Oversee landlord compliance across key areas, including fire safety, gas, electrical safety, asbestos, water hygiene, lifts, emergency lighting and alarm systems.
  • Lead the management of damp, mould and other property-related hazards, ensuring timely intervention and compliance with relevant legislation, including Awaab's Law.
  • Ensure Housing Health and Safety Rating System (HHSRS) risks are identified, monitored and appropriately addressed.
  • Develop and implement effective compliance strategies, policies and procedures.
  • Manage and develop operational teams, ensuring high standards of performance, accountability and service delivery.
  • Oversee budgets, business planning and resource allocation, ensuring value for money.
  • Drive continuous improvement, operational efficiency and positive change across the service.
  • Monitor performance, identify emerging risks and provide reports and recommendations to senior management.
  • Work collaboratively with internal departments, contractors, regulatory bodies and external stakeholders.
  • Promote a strong health and safety culture, ensuring resident safety remains central to all decisions.


The successful candidate will have:

  • Significant senior management experience within housing maintenance, property compliance, asset management or a similar operational environment.
  • A degree-level qualification and/or membership of a relevant professional body.
  • Proven experience managing teams, budgets and complex operational services.
  • Strong knowledge of statutory and regulatory requirements relating to housing safety and compliance.
  • Experience overseeing multiple areas of property compliance and risk management.
  • A track record of business planning, change management and continuous service improvement.
  • Experience and/or qualifications in Health & Safety.
  • Excellent leadership, communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • The ability to make informed, risk-based decisions and deliver results within a demanding operational environment.

What's on Offer?

Alongside a competitive salary, the organisation offers an attractive benefits package, including:

  • Local Government Pension Scheme.
  • Generous annual leave and sick pay entitlements.
  • Flexible and hybrid working opportunities.
  • Professional development and career progression opportunities.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.
  • Subsidised leisure facilities and wellbeing benefits.
  • Cycle to Work scheme.
  • Public transport and parking benefits.


This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced housing or property compliance professional to take on a senior leadership position, influence service delivery and help ensure residents live in safe, well-maintained homes.

If your application is unsuccessful on this occasion, we may keep your CV on file for future opportunities.

job.title: Fire Safety Manager
job.description:
Fire Safety Manager
Ipswich
(£53,051 – £55,224 per annum)

We are looking for a Fire Safety Manager to join a public sector organisation and lead their fire safety compliance across a diverse property portfolio, ensuring all buildings meet relevant fire safety legislation, regulatory requirements and organisational policies.

The role is responsible for maintaining a safe environment for residents, customers, visitors and staff, while overseeing fire safety programmes, risk management and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities as a Fire Safety Manager:

  • Lead and manage fire safety compliance, ensuring adherence to the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, Fire Safety Act 2021 and Building Safety Act 2022.
  • Manage and develop a team of fire safety professionals, providing leadership, technical guidance, training and performance management.
  • Oversee fire risk assessments, ensuring identified actions are prioritised, allocated, completed and appropriately recorded.
  • Develop and implement building-specific fire strategies and organisation-wide fire safety policies.
  • Lead fire safety improvement programmes, managing significant budgets, contractors, consultants and procurement processes.
  • Ensure statutory fire safety inspections, testing and maintenance are completed, including fire doors, alarms, emergency lighting, firefighting equipment and sprinkler systems.
  • Maintain accurate fire safety records and ensure compliance information is accessible and up to date.
  • Liaise with fire and rescue services, regulatory bodies, contractors and internal stakeholders, responding to audits and addressing any areas of non-compliance.
  • Oversee fire safety projects from initial assessment and design through to procurement, delivery and completion.
  • Develop resident engagement and communication strategies to promote fire safety awareness and ensure appropriate support for vulnerable residents.
  • Monitor budgets, contracts, performance and service delivery, ensuring value for money and high standards of workmanship.
  • Provide professional fire safety advice, prepare management reports and present compliance updates to senior management.
  • Lead service improvements, review working practices and develop procedures to strengthen long-term fire safety management.
  • Ensure appropriate controls are in place for maintenance and building works to protect fire safety measures and compartmentation.
  • Support wider health and safety responsibilities and maintain professional competence through ongoing training.

Experience and Expertise required:

  • Degree-level qualification or equivalent professional qualification in a relevant building-related discipline, with substantial post-qualification experience.
  • At least five years' relevant technical or professional experience.
  • Strong experience managing fire safety within residential or property environments.
  • In-depth knowledge of fire safety legislation, regulations and compliance requirements.
  • Proven ability to identify and manage fire risks, undertake fire risk assessments and develop appropriate fire strategies.
  • Experience planning and delivering fire safety improvement programmes across multiple sites.
  • Strong organisational, project management and prioritisation skills, with the ability to manage competing deadlines, budgets and resources.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to engage with stakeholders at all levels.
  • A proactive, risk-based approach to problem-solving, with the ability to develop practical and innovative solutions.
  • Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.

Desirable Requirements:

  • IFE Level 4 Certificate in Fire Safety or equivalent.
  • NEBOSH Certificate in Fire Safety.
  • Experience presenting technical information and advice to senior management and external stakeholders.


If your application is unsuccessful on this occasion, we may retain your CV and personal details for consideration for future suitable opportunities.

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
KC Group is partnering with an ambitious, growing SME group with businesses operating across multiple sectors. As the group enters its next phase of expansion, we’re looking for a commercially astute Finance Manager who can look beyond the numbers and play a key role in shaping business strategy and driving growth.

This is a high-impact opportunity for a forward-thinking finance professional to work closely with the Managing Director, take ownership of the finance function and influence key commercial decisions. You will lead the evolution from a transactional finance operation to a proactive, insight-led function, strengthening financial visibility, supporting strategic initiatives and building the infrastructure needed to scale.

This is much more than a traditional Finance Manager role. You will combine strong financial control with commercial insight, strategic planning and forward-looking analysis to help the group make better decisions and capitalise on opportunities.

Key responsibilities will include:

  1. Strategic Finance & FP&A: Lead budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling and scenario planning to support business growth and long-term strategy.
  2. Commercial Business Partnering: Work closely with the MD and leadership team to evaluate performance, challenge assumptions and identify opportunities to improve profitability and margins.
  3. Growth & M&A Support: Support acquisition opportunities, business expansion and strategic initiatives through financial analysis, modelling and commercial evaluation.
  4. Financial Reporting: Own monthly management accounts, delivering meaningful commentary on performance, risks, opportunities and variances.
  5. Cash Flow & Working Capital: Improve cash flow forecasting, stock management and debtor control to support informed decisions and sustainable growth.
  6. Financial Leadership: Lead and develop a small finance team, strengthening processes, controls and accountability as the group scales.
  7. Systems & Process Improvement: Enhance reporting, data visibility and financial systems, including supporting the implementation of Unleashed alongside Xero.
  8. Commercial Performance: Analyse pricing, margins, product profitability and supplier costs, identifying opportunities to drive efficiency and improve returns.


We are looking to speak with people who have a commercial and strategic mindset who can combine financial expertise with the confidence to influence decisions.

Experience required:

  1. Experience as a Finance Manager, Financial Controller or in a similar commercially focused finance role.
  2. Strong FP&A experience, including budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling and scenario analysis.
  3. A track record of supporting business growth, strategic planning or change within an SME or entrepreneurial environment.
  4. Experience supporting acquisitions, M&A activity or business expansion, or a strong interest and capability in this area.
  5. The ability to translate financial data into clear, actionable commercial insight.
  6. Confidence partnering with senior leadership and influencing non-finance stakeholders.
  7. A proactive, hands-on approach, with the ability to build processes and improve financial infrastructure as a business grows.

ACA, ACCA or CIMA qualified, part-qualified or qualified by experience candidates will be considered. Experience in a product-led, manufacturing, FMCG or stock-intensive business would be advantageous.

Benefits and Key details:

  1. 33 days’ holiday, including bank holidays.
  2. Flexible working hours, with core hours of 10:00am–4:30pm.
  3. Direct exposure to the Managing Director and involvement in strategic decision-making.
  4. The opportunity to influence growth, commercial performance and future business direction.
  5. A clear progression pathway towards Financial Controller.
  6. A collaborative, entrepreneurial environment where initiative, ownership and fresh thinking are valued.

This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious finance professional who wants to move beyond reporting the numbers and play a genuine role in driving business performance, growth and strategy.

If your CV isn't shortlisted on this occasion, we will keep your details on file for other suitable roles.
